title: MCP–MeAsp chip benchmark with a linear initial field and finite boundary exchange

categories.literature: supported by literature, as relayed by the team's GPT-assisted check; the cited papers are not recorded here
categories.assumed: assumption, design choice or numerical setting

length_um.source: The planned chip is 4000 um long; shortened 10x so a run finishes in minutes. The 800 x 200 um cross-section is kept because the wall-to-volume ratio sets how often cells meet a wall.

width_um.source: Team chip design (0.8 mm). No measured cross-section yet.

height_um.source: Team chip design (0.2 mm). No measured cross-section yet.

grid_spacing_um.source: Numerical grid choice. Finite boundary relaxation and diffusion evolve the field; refinement is part of first-release checks.

low_uM.source: Team plan: 0 uM MeAsp on the low side. The gradient is taken as already established and stationary; the real agar-gel chip needs time to establish it.

high_uM.source: Team plan: 200 uM MeAsp on the high side (200 uM/mm over 1 mm in the planned chip; here 0.25 uM/um over 800 um).

background_uM.source: Zero-gradient control: the mean of the gradient condition, so receptors see the same average concentration.

diffusivity_um2_s.source: Team estimate 8e-6 cm^2/s without a recorded primary source. Diffusion remains active; boundary exchange is finite.

boundary_rate_s.source: Numerical device: first-order relaxation rate that holds the outermost grid layer at the side-channel concentration. No physical counterpart.

n_cells.source: Simulation size. Cells do not interact chemically here, so density does not change the result except through collisions.

cell_length_um.source: Typical E. coli size; constructed example value, not measured.

cell_diameter_um.source: Typical E. coli size; constructed example value, not measured.

speed_um_s.source: GPT-assisted literature check (2026-10-03): swimming speed about 20-25 um/s. Citation not recorded.

minimum_tumble_rate_s.source: Constructed bound. The literature check found no experimental basis for this bound; unstimulated tumble rate is about 1/s.

maximum_tumble_rate_s.source: Constructed bound, same status as the minimum.

tumble_mode.source: Tumble is an instantaneous reorientation; the dwell time is not modelled.

turn_kernel.source: New heading uniform on the sphere. Model A's source uses a mean turn angle near 68 deg (docs/science/n3-mechanisms.md). Open question.

cluster_size.source: GPT-assisted literature check (2026-10-03): fits near 6 reported; effective size depends on the model and receptor state. Citation not recorded.

inactive_binding_um.source: GPT-assisted literature check (2026-10-03): about 18-20 uM for Tar-MeAsp, attributed to a 2013 quantitative chemotaxis modelling study. Do not mix with a 20/500 uM set from another study. Citation not recorded.

active_binding_um.source: GPT-assisted literature check (2026-10-03): 500-3000 uM depending on the model; paired here with Ki=18 uM, which the check attributed to the same study. Citation not recorded.

methylation_energy.source: Reduced units: methylation m is dimensionless and adaptation_rate_s is defined in these units.

methylation_reference.source: Gauge choice for the reduced methylation coordinate.

baseline_activity.source: Model baseline assumption (about 1/3), judged acceptable by the literature check.

adaptation_rate_s.source: Not fitted. Chosen because the single-cell small-signal kernel (positive lobe peaks near 1.3 s, negative lobe decays over about 3 s) is closest to Segall et al. 1986 (about 1 s positive, 3 s negative, as relayed by the literature check). Scanned at 0.1, 0.3 and 1.

motor_hill.source: Constructed. Models A and B use h about 10.3 and KM about 3.1 uM (Cluzel 2000). The difference is unresolved.

dt_s.source: Numerical setting. Earlier 8-seed comparison was reported by the team; not treated as validation in this release.
